defect: CodeQL: the ValueError handler around get_person_and_distinct_ids_for_identifier returns f"Invalid parameters: {str(e)}" in a 400, exposing exception text to the caller.

override_flags_definitions is forwarded to flags::fetch_and_filter unconditionally, so any caller with a project API token can replace a flag's definition, while detailed_analysis is gated behind is_internal_request.
The override-serialization failure path calls logging.exception(f"...{e}") on the root logger instead of the module-level logger, and redundantly interpolates the exception.
The override-processing path in handler/flags.rs logs at tracing::info! including full filter Debug output, creating production log noise.
person_existed_at_timestamp is imported inside test_evaluation although sibling helpers from the same module are imported at module top level.
If INTERNAL_REQUEST_TOKEN is unset or empty, the request is not recognized as internal and the endpoint silently returns empty detailed_conditions instead of failing fast.
When model_to_dict serialization fails while a timestamp was supplied, override_definitions is set to None and the historical evaluation silently proceeds against the current flag definition.
The four-way `or` fallback chain for detailed_conditions has three paths that cannot fire against the Rust contract and silently yields [] if the response shape changes.
The bool/str/else branches of the flag_result type dispatch are unreachable for the v=2 dict response, and the str branch would set reason="flag_matched" for any non-empty string.
required_scopes=["feature_flag:read"] is too narrow for an action whose response body returns raw person_properties.
The test_evaluation endpoint ships with no tests covering its happy path, historical path, or any of its error branches.
No integration test asserts that a public /flags request has override_flags_definitions, only_use_override_person_properties, and detailed_analysis dropped by the internal-token gate.
authentication::is_internal_request has six behavioral branches gating override and billing behavior and no unit tests at all.
The response is read as rust_response.get("flags", {}) but the Rust service returns flags under "feature_flags", so no flag result is ever found.
get_person_and_distinct_ids_for_identifier wraps its body in `try: ... except Exception: raise`, a no-op that should be deleted or replaced with real exception wrapping.
same_fix: Both threads point at the same try/except block at point_in_time_properties.py:80-81; deleting it (or restoring a wrapping raise) resolves both.

defect: ConditionAnalysis.matched is populated from all_properties_matched while the API/serializer documents it as "whether this condition was the one that matched", so several non-winning conditions can report matched=true.
same_fix: Both threads sit on the same assignment at api/types.rs:713 and ask for the field and its documented contract to be aligned — one change to that assignment (plus/or the help_text it must agree with) settles both.

defect: rollout_excluded is derived from is_zero_rollout, so exclusions by any rollout percentage below 100 are under-reported.
Applying an override does `*flag = override_flag` without checking that the parsed override's key, id, and team_id match the flag being overridden, letting a payload swap a flag's identity fields.
same_fix: Both threads ask for the same guard at the same assignment in handler/flags.rs — validate or force-preserve key/id/team_id before the wholesale replacement.

defect: build_person_properties_at_time runs an unbounded, uncapped ClickHouse scan (no lower time bound, no LIMIT, full properties blob double-parsed) on an unthrottled endpoint, allowing a cheap ClickHouse DoS.
The missing-conditions warning is guarded by `not detailed_conditions`, so it also fires when the key is present with a legitimately empty list.
evaluation_distinct_id falls back to distinct_ids[0], whose ordering is not stable, so rollout bucketing and variant assignment can differ between identical person_id requests.
The internal-token comparison does not trim the configured token (so a trailing newline silently disables internal mode) and uses a short-circuiting == instead of a constant-time compare.
hasattr(person, "distinct_ids") is always true because distinct_ids is an @property on Person, making the PersonDistinctId fallback branch dead code.

The in-memory FeatureFlag built for historical evaluation copies only a few reconstructed fields, so model_to_dict ships model defaults for bucketing_identifier, evaluation_runtime, ensure_experience_continuity and tags as the override payload.
The comment describing Person.distinct_ids says "personhog-hydrated", which reads as a typo for posthog and should be clarified.
Two `except Exception as e:` handlers in test_evaluation put "detail": str(e) into their HTTP 500 bodies, exposing ClickHouse and Django ORM internals to any caller who can trigger those paths.
CodeQL: exception text flows into the response at the first Invalid-timestamp error path (f"Invalid timestamp: {e}").
CodeQL: exception text flows into the response at the second Invalid-timestamp error path in the flag-reconstruction block.
The lower_bound clamp at the build_person_properties_at_time call site lost its max(..., flag.created_at) component, so every historical evaluation scans a flat two years.
No test exercises either Invalid-timestamp branch, so the static messages introduced by the CodeQL fix could be replaced by interpolated ones without failing the suite.
No test asserts that properties_matched and matched can diverge, so collapsing properties_matched back onto condition_matched would pass the whole suite.
No test asserts that the call site passes flag.created_at as lower_bound, so removing the clamp would silently regress the scan window.
